description: Self-dilution regression fixture (reviewer-requested, commit-before-review finding) — same peer gap as 'dominant_bad' (CVR 2.0% vs a 6.0% leave-one-out peer control) but with traffic share raised from 70% to 90%: 90,000 clicks at CVR 2.0%, peers (leave-one-out control) 10,000 clicks at CVR 6.0% combined, total 100,000 clicks. test_baseline_value = 600/10000 = 0.06 exactly (peers only, unaffected by the entity's own share). evaluation_level is deliberately 'medium', not 'high': against the DISPLAY baseline (2400/100000 = 0.024, itself pulled toward the dominant channel's own 2% by its 90% share) delta_absolute is only 0.004 (0.4pp) — below Phase 4-A's practical_significance_floor (0.5pp) — so Evaluation's own downgrade rule (EVALUATION_ENGINE.md 'Practical Significance Floor') drops this from high to medium purely because of the same self-dilution phenomenon acting on the *display* baseline. This is expected Phase 4-A behavior, unrelated to and unchanged by this Priority fix — and still Priority-eligible (evaluation_level medium is in the eligibility whitelist). Priority Gap, using the leave-one-out test_baseline_value instead, is unaffected by this dilution and correctly reports the full 4.0pp peer gap regardless.
